newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Mubarak gives blunt riposte to EU envoy.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak gives blunt riposte to EU envoy.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak gave a blunt riposte on Monday to remarks attributed to the European Union's Middle East envoy -- another sign that not all is well between the two mediating parties.

Asked about a report that the European Union and the United States had agreed to give Egypt two more weeks to revive negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians, Mubarak said: "The European envoy has no right to give Egypt a deadline to make progress in the peace process.
"We don't work for him and I'd like to give him a year or two to see how clever he is," he told reporters.

He was referring to European Union envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos, who met U.S. envoy Dennis Ross in Washington to coordinate U.S. and European attempts to break the deadlock in substantial Israeli-Palestinian talks.

Israeli Radio on Sunday quoted Moratinos as saying that if Egypt's efforts failed within the two weeks then the United States, in conjunction with the European Union, would engage in "comprehensive crisis intervention".
After talks in Cairo last week, Moratinos and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa gave a very different assessment of the chances of a breakthrough in the mediation.
Moratinos said he saw the beginnings of a solution to Israeli-Palestinian disputes and some openness on the part of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

But Moussa said: "It's far too early to be talking about openings especially after the statements made by Israel, and these are statements that are very damaging to any initiative and any action that can lead to an easing (in the situation)."

Moussa was reacting to a report that Netanyahu had spelled out for the first time his vision of a permanent peace settlement. Israel would keep key areas in the occupied West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem, which is claimed by both Israel and the Palestinians.
